newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya's Moi says weekly coffee auction to stay.
newsitem.headline: Kenya's Moi says weekly coffee auction to stay.

text.p: Kenyan President Daniel arap Moi said on Friday a weekly export auction would remain the only method of selling Kenyan coffee and gave greater autonomy to the Coffee Board of Kenya (CBK) as the main marketing agency.

A number of industry players, including main millers Kenya Planters' Cooperative Union and Thika Coffee Mills, have in recent weeks asked the government to allow other agencies to market coffee. Moi said this would distort marketing.
Moi also confirmed the end of a monopoly in coffee milling, saying that farmers had the right to choose which milling company would handle their crop "to enhance efficiency".
Moi spoke at an agricultural fair in the key growing town of Nyeri, 200 km (125 miles) north of the capital Nairobi.
"The Coffee Board shall continue to market coffee through the central auction," Moi said, adding that the decision had been made on the recommendations of a government task force.

The task force, created by the agriculture minister and which submitted its report in May, favoured the auctions as the best way to protect the quality of Kenyan coffee and safeguard a tradition of trust between Kenya and global consumers.
Moi said the government had adopted the recommendations.
Coffee lies behind tourism and tea as a leading Kenyan foreign exchange earner. It led that category until 1987.
Some 300,000 smallholders produce an estimated 65 percent of Kenya's coffee and are responsible for its high quality, the Coffee Board of Kenya says. Estates produce just 35 percent.
